title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-v6
content:
Notes to self - rough unit economics and tier ideas (back-of-envelope).

Context / goal:
- Quick sketch for hosted API pricing / tiering for next engineering review. Focus: simple, predictable, and PLG-friendly. Need numbers that map to cost per token + margin + simple tiers.
- Keep defaults conservative; we can tune after small rollout.

Assumptions:
- GPU serving cost (amortized infra + ops) per effective token: approx $0.0000025/token for large seq (this is blended across batching + KV cache). (i.e. $2.5 per million tokens).  <-- double-check with infra team.
- Model license / weights cost: negligible for open models; add small ops surcharge for audited models: $0.0000005/token.
- Embedding cost (compute + storage) per vector: ~$0.0005 per embedding compute + $0.00002 per vector-month storage (we charge monthly separately)
- Average call profile (target customers): interactive chat sessions: 1200 tokens in + 800 tokens out per session (2k total). Batch embedding jobs: 100k vectors/day at scale customer.
- Overhead (auth, routing, logging, monitoring): add 10% on top of compute cost.

Base cost calc (per 1M tokens):
- serving compute: $2.50
- ops/license: $0.50
- overhead (10%): $0.30
- total cost ~= $3.30 per 1M tokens => $0.0000033/token.

Target gross margin: 70% (SaaS-y) => price per 1M tokens = cost / (1 - 0.7) = $3.30 / 0.3 = $11.00 per 1M tokens. Round to $10-12.

Simpler pricing unit: $0.01 per 1k tokens = $10 per 1M tokens. Matches target.

Tier ideas (consumer + startup + business + enterprise):
- Free / Trial: 100k tokens/month free for signups (short-term experimentation).
- Starter: $10/month -> includes 1M tokens (billed monthly). Good for prototypes, low commitment.
- Growth: $100/month -> includes 12M tokens + 100k embeddings/month (bundled). Effective token price ~ $8.3 per M.
- Scale: $1,000/month -> includes 140M tokens + 1.5M embeddings/month. Unit price ~ $7.14 per M.
- Enterprise: custom committed pricing with reserved capacity (Dedicated). Discounting based on commit; typical baseline $4-6 per M with SLA + support.

Notes on embedding pricing:
- Charge per embedding compute + optional storage retention fee.
- Compute: $0.0005 per embedding (e.g., $0.50 per 1k vectors).
- Storage: $0.00002 per vector-month (e.g., 1M vectors => $20/month storage).
- Offer bundled embeddings in Growth/Scale tiers with discounts (20-40% off per-vector compute).

Function / tool-calls / structured outputs:
- Some customers will use lots of short calls (high QPS, small tokens). Need a QPS surcharge or minimums?
- Idea: include a small per-request fee for tiny calls under 50 tokens: $0.0005 per request to offset RPC overhead. But risk: friction / complexity.
- Alternative: include request-count in quotas for free/trial only. For paid tiers ignore per-request fees for simplicity.

Bursting / Dedicated / Private:
- Dedicated reserved capacity: monthly commit model. Price = base token price * commit multiplier with discounts based on duration / size. Also include infrastructure surcharge to reflect dedicated infra ops.
- Private/VPC: charge platform fee + per-token for usage if using Redwood managed runtime. For on-prem fully customer-managed, license + support fee (flat).

Promotions and PLG considerations:
- First 30 days: double free quota for signups that connect credit card (improve conversion).
- Growth credits for open-source projects / academia.
- Marketplace listing: list Starter & Growth with clear SKU.

Edge cases / questions to resolve:
- What is accurate blended cost-per-token after batching and KV caching on our hosted fleet? Need infra numbers: 95p/50p percentiles.
- Cost differences by model size (7B vs 70B) -> Should be different unit prices or same list price but model weighting?
  - Option A: single token price but charge model multipliers (e.g., 7B x1, 70B x2.5). Simpler for customers?
  - Option B: separate model SKUs (text-7B, text-70B) with explicit per-token prices. Cleaner revenue tracking.
- Handling streaming vs non-streaming for token accounting (include all tokens generated).
- Rate limiting and QPS gating for Starter tier to prevent abuse (e.g., 5 rps).

Quick sample scenarios:
- Indie app: Starter $10/mo, 1M tokens. If they use 1M tokens -> price per token $0.00001 = $10 per million -> matches. Our cost ~ $3.3 per M => gross margin ~67%. OK.
- Mid-market SaaS: Growth $100/mo, 12M tokens -> $8.33 per M. Cost margin ~60-65% -> reasonable.
- High-volume enterprise: 1B tokens/month at $5 per M -> $5,000/month cost to customer; we get margin depending on cost at scale (maybe cost drops to $1.5 per M after pooling, still good).

Implementation notes for billing system:
- Bill per token rounded to nearest 1k tokens monthly; include overage charges beyond tier allowance at pay-as-you-go rate (e.g., $10 per M).
- Track embeddings separately and bill monthly as a line item.
- Support per-model multipliers in billing metering (if we adopt multipliers).

Unresolved pricing mechanics (action items):
- Get infra cost report: real blended cost per 1M tokens (by model family). -> @Rajan
- Decide model pricing strategy: multipliers vs model SKUs -> sync with product + finance. -> schedule quick meeting.
- Confirm embedding storage cost with infra/storage billing. -> @Olivia

Rough TL;DR to share in sync:
- Suggested public list price: $0.01 per 1k tokens ($10 per 1M) as base with tiering (Starter/Growth/Scale) and enterprise reserved pricing $4-6 per M. Embeddings billed separately ($0.50 per 1k vectors compute; storage per vector-month).
- Keep billing simple for PLG: bundle tokens into Starter/Growth; overage at base rate.

End of scratchpad.

Random notes / brain dump (incomplete):
- Consider adding a "token credits" gift for developers who open-source library integrations.
- Might test per-request fee in a small cohort (to measure overhead impact) but don't roll out broadly.
- Need legal + finance signoff before marketing numbers.

-- Maya
